item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q020_syntaxin_fragment_reclassification","answer":"In current public SCOPe 2.08, the `1br0` and `1ez3` syntaxin entries are not evidence for a separate fragment-only fold. `1br0` is `d1br0a_`, and `1ez3` chains `A`, `B`, and `C` are `d1ez3a_`, `d1ez3b_`, and `d1ez3c_`; all four are classified as `a.47.2.1` in class `a` All alpha proteins, fold `a.47` STAT-like, superfamily `a.47.2` t-snare proteins, and family `a.47.2.1` t-snare proteins, under the Syntaxin 1A N-terminal-domain protein node `sunid` 47663. SCOPe explicitly flags each `1br0`/`1ez3` domain as a \"three-helical fragment; similar to one spectrin repeat\" and marks it with the `ms` inconsistency, meaning it is missing secondary structures that made up less than one-third of the common domain. So a match to these records should be read as a local, incomplete view of the Syntaxin 1A N-terminal/Habc domain within the t-SNARE family, not as a complete-domain template and not as permission to transfer all syntaxin-domain architecture or function from a single three-helix fragment. `1dn1` chain `B` is also classified as `d1dn1b_`, `a.47.2.1`, but in SCOPe 2.08 it sits under `automated matches` and is annotated as an automated match to `d3c98b_`; `3c98` chain `B` is the non-obsolete full-domain Syntaxin 1A N-terminal entry in the same `a.47.2.1` lineage. The other domain in the `1dn1` Sec1/syntaxin complex, chain `A`, is a Sec1/munc18-like SM protein in `e.25.1.1`, so its classification must not be merged into the syntaxin chain.
